summary: Sweden is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (as of 30 December 2025) can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else applies for a €90 Schengen short-stay visa through the Swedish Migration Agency's consular network.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

European Commission (Migration and Home Affairs) — Applying for a Schengen visa

fee.text: Applicants shall pay a visa fee of EUR 90.

processing.text: That period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases, notably when further scrutiny of the application is needed.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa. Such an extension shall be granted free of charge. 2. The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa may be extended if the visa holder provides proof of serious personal reasons justifying the extension of the period of validity or the duration of stay.

name.text: Citizens of certain non-EU countries must hold a short-stay visa when travelling to the Schengen area.

method.text: An application shall be examined and decided on by the consulate of the competent Member State in whose jurisdiction the applicant legally resides.

declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance; the EU says registration can be quicker if you register some data beforehand at a self-service kiosk or through a national app, where available. The UK government's travel advice says there is no cost for EES registration.

tips.text: Bring a debit or credit card: the UK government's travel advice says many shops, cafes and restaurants in Sweden do not accept cash.

Under Sweden's Alcohol Act (2010:1622), retail sale of spirits, wine and strong beer is reserved for a state-owned company (Systembolaget), apart from the limited farm sales the Act allows, and alcoholic drinks may not be sold to anyone under 20 (18 for low-strength folköl), although licensed bars and restaurants may serve them to people aged 18 and over.

Canada's travel advice says the right of public access (allemansrätten) lets you move and camp on public land, but not within 70 m of a dwelling or cultivated land, and that some areas, seasons and uses are restricted.

The UK government's travel advice says snow and ice cause road accidents daily in winter, and that all vehicles must have winter tyres from 1 December to 31 March and at any other time the police designate.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Sweden?
faq.answer: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely with a passport or ID card. Nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (as of 30 December 2025) — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa applied for via the Swedish mission serving their place of residence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Sweden?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Sweden and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Sweden Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11, and allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. For visits of more than 90 days, the Swedish Migration Agency says you need a visitor's residence permit.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Sweden?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once ETIAS starts, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding.

faq.question: Can I pay with cash in Sweden?
faq.answer: Often not. The UK government's travel advice says many shops, cafes and restaurants do not accept cash, so make sure you have a debit or credit card with you, and Canada's travel advice says many shops and restaurants no longer accept cash.
